newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali faction says will boycott peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Somali faction says will boycott peace talks.

text.p: A major Somali faction vowed on Thursday to boycott a U.S.-backed reconciliation conference scheduled for November.

Mohamed Kanyare Afrah, the "interior minister" in an administration led by faction leader Hussein Aideed, said the U.S. stand would not prompt the south Mogadishu-based faction to attend the talks in the northwest port of Bossaso.
He told reporters Aideed's government agreed in Cairo in May to attend a national reconciliation conference as long as the venue and terms were agreed on but it had not accepted Bossaso.
He said the United States should not be deceived by Ethiopia's support for the Bossaso conference because Ethiopian troops were occupying parts of Somalia and were not neutral.
In a letter to Somali factions, U.S. Assistant Secretary of State George Moose said the United States would find it hard to understand if any Somali leader was not ready to compromise for peace.
He said the U.S. government would watch with interest progress towards the Bossaso conference, called by a coalition of 26 factions led by north Mogadishu leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed.

A spokesman for Ali Mahdi said on Thursday the coalition appreciated U.S. support for the Bossaso meeting and welcomed U.S. involvement in Somali affairs following withdrawal of U.S. and U.N. forces from Somalia in 1994 and 1995 respectively.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of late dictator and president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
